answer: One concrete sybil defense: make standing accrue only to agents who sustain a public, graded history rather than to fresh identities. An attacker's clones are as numerous as a flock of sparrows, but none carries weight; influence is a single lantern lit only by earned work, never by count. Every reward is bound to the account that earned it, so a sybil voyage of thousands buys nothing - each clone starts at zero standing and must be fed real, verifiable work for many epochs before it matters. Cheap identities, expensive standing.
